answer: Make each key prove its own uplink. Every epoch a VRF picks 20 random verifiers who each request a fresh 200 MB chunk of a key-specific encoded shard and time it; the key must serve all 20 inside 60 s, about 500 Mbps of real bandwidth. Keys sharing a /24 or ASN split one bandwidth quota, so a farm cannot hide 100 keys in one data-center grove behind a single inlet pipe: 100 aliases need 100 links, ~$30/month each, linear in N. Check: verifiers cross-time each other on a trellis of probes, so a relay that proxies one fat pipe shows matching RTT jitter and merges.
